output.name: Thavesk
output.myth: Aun built a boat of cloth and bone and sailed it south, past the last island, because he wanted to see where the wind stopped. The water tilted under him. He kept on until the pole was behind his back and the cold stars hung upside down. Mother Hesk saw him go and wound a little more string. Tavo the Gale came up under the stern and laughed. The wind did not let him turn. Aun went all the way round the bottom of the world, and there was his own wake waiting ahead, going the same way he was going. Óllun, the Boat That Turned Back, had turned in the smooth dark water and watched him pass. At the Unpaid Crossing the grey boatman wanted a shell coin, and Aun had none, so he was ferried over for nothing and cursed it. Kael still casts for that wake and never catches it. If you see two lamps in the Unflown chasing each other, that is Aun's boat and its trail. Do not wave at them. They are not yet home.
output.finding: Sailors far south find Thavesk by sighting Óllun, the Boat That Turned Back, low in the west and then looking one hand-span (about 20°) further south of it, where two lamps chase each other in the dark.
